control_name: Format-String-Safe API Enforcement (Compile-Time and Runtime Format Validation)
description: Prevent exploitation of format string vulnerabilities by enforcing format-string-safe API usage across compiled and interpreted codebases. In C/C++, enable compiler diagnostics that reject non-literal format arguments (-Wformat-security, -Werror=format-security, /analyze on MSVC) and replace printf-family calls that accept user-controlled format specifiers with fixed-format alternatives (snprintf with literal format, or positional/typed formatting APIs). In managed languages, use parameterized logging (SLF4J {}, Python %s with logging module, .NET structured logging) instead of string interpolation with user input in format position. At the build system level, enforce these checks as CI gate failures so that format-string-unsafe patterns cannot merge. This control directly blocks the attacker's ability to use format specifiers (%n, %x, %s) to read or write arbitrary memory, leak stack contents, or achieve code execution via controlled writes.

conditions: Requires all source compiled with format-security warnings promoted to errors
Managed-language codebases must use parameterized logging APIs rather than string concatenation in format position
CI enforcement prevents regression — without gating, developers can introduce new format-string-unsafe patterns

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: The attacker must find a code path where a user-controlled string reaches a format-specifier-interpreting function without compile-time or runtime neutralization — format-security compiler flags and parameterized APIs eliminate the most common paths, forcing the attacker to find an uncovered edge case or bypass the CI gate

Format string read primitives (%x, %s for stack/heap disclosure) are blocked because user input cannot inject format specifiers into printf-family calls — information disclosure is limited to what the application explicitly outputs

relationships.rationale: Directly prevents use of externally-controlled format strings by enforcing literal-only format arguments at compile time and parameterized APIs at runtime

verification.method: Verify that C/C++ build configurations enable format-string-security compiler warnings as errors, and that CI pipelines gate on these warnings. For managed languages, review logging configuration to confirm parameterized formatting is enforced.

commands.expected: Build files contain -Wformat-security and -Werror=format-security (or MSVC /analyze equivalent)
error: format not a string literal and no format arguments [-Werror=format-security]
No hits — all printf-family calls use literal format strings

remediation.name: RPM global build macros with format-security enforcement

steps.description: Create an RPM macros drop-in that appends -Wformat-security and -Werror=format-security to the default compiler flags for all RPM builds on this system. This ensures any package rebuilt locally will reject non-literal format strings at compile time.

remediation.name: GCC specs file override for system-wide format-security enforcement

steps.description: Dump the current GCC specs to a temporary file as a baseline for modification

Install a modified GCC specs file that injects -Wformat-security -Werror=format-security into every compilation. All gcc invocations on this system will enforce format-string safety by default. WARNING: this affects all compilations system-wide; some third-party code may fail to compile if it uses non-literal format strings.
Clean up the temporary specs baseline file
Add format-security compiler options to the top-level CMakeLists.txt if not already present. This enforces the control for all targets in the CMake project.

references.source: CWE-134: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
